transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doc. Well, I guess what finally got me in here is that over these past few months, my mind just keeps jumping around. 

I drive a truck for a living, and lately, it feels like every little thing pulls my attention away—a chirp on the CB radio, a fuel price sign out the window, or just some random new idea that pops into my head. Because of it, I'm missing details I normally never miss. I'll completely overlook a client’s delivery note, or I'll forget who I promised to call back. I'm usually pretty sharp with that stuff, but I just can't seem to stay on track right now.
Along with this distractibility, have you also noticed any changes in your mood or energy—like feeling unusually upbeat, irritable, or needing much less sleep than usual?

Yeah, I have. For months now, it's been... well, I've been either way too fired up, just feeling like everything is going to work out perfectly no matter what. Or on the flip side, I'll find myself snapping over really small stuff at home and out in the yard. That really isn't my usual way of acting, but it's just been happening a lot lately.
Did you notice these mood and attention changes starting fairly recently, as a clear shift from how you normally are, or have you had similar attention difficulties since childhood?

No, it's definitely a recent thing. I never really had trouble paying attention when I was younger or anything like that, so this is a clear shift from how I normally am. 

I'd say this has all been going on for about seven months now. It started right around the time my daughter moved back home, and I started trying to keep everything steady around the house. That's really when I noticed things changing.

Before these past seven months, have you ever had a period—lasting a week or more—where you felt unusually depressed, low, or hopeless, or another time where you felt abnormally high, energetic, or irritable like this?

No, I can't say that I have. Before this year, I was always pretty steady. I've never really had any times where I felt super depressed or hopeless for weeks on end. And I definitely haven't had this kind of wired, irritable feeling before either. Like I said, it's really just been since my daughter came back that everything started getting out of whack. Before that, I was just my regular self.

These symptoms represent a clear departure from his baseline personality and functioning, with no prior manic, hypomanic, or depressive episodes, and no childhood history of inattention (ruling out ADHD).
